page: Microsoft Azure E4-2as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB per core, alongside 66 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% in stress-ng tests, while single-threaded text processing and decompression benchmarks score in the average range. Conversely, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng and the bottom 10% for Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds ranking in the bottom 25%, and small-block cached reads in the bottom 10%.

This hardware profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring a high memory footprint relative to compute resources, avoiding the expense of provisioning excess vCPUs. However, the low core count and limited memory bandwidth result in poor performance for database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving, which all rank in the bottom 10%. The server is best suited for memory-bound, single-threaded applications, lightweight caching, and basic data processing tasks that do not demand high parallel processing or intensive memory throughput.
